podcast.body: A "huge hit" in 1995, this song from the album *Different Class* was inspired by an experience Jarvis Cocker had with Sophia Focca, a wealthy student at St. Martin's College of Art and Design who engaged in "slumming" with less affluent students. Cocker embellished her attitude for artistic effect. "The song was based on an experience Jarvis Cocker had had with a fellow student at St. Martin's College of Art and Design. Her name, apparently, was Sophia Focca."

podcast.body: A comic strip based on the story told in this song was illustrated by Jamie Hewlett in 1995. This comic book version was made available with the French single and an Australian box set of the song. "That's Pulp and Common People, which came with a comic book version of the story told in song, but only for the French version of the single and an Australian box set."

podcast.body: Released on their 1995 album "Different Class," "Common People" is described as Pulp's biggest hit. Its lyrical construction, especially its observational style, was a significant influence on the Arctic Monkeys.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The first single from the *Different Class* album, which became a huge hit for Britpop in the summer of 1995. The song was based on Jarvis Cocker's actual experience with a fellow student, Sophia Focca, at St. Martin's College of Art and Design, who came from a well-off family but seemed to be interested in "slumming" with her schoolmates. "The song was based on an actual experience Jarvis Cocker had with a fellow student at St. Martin's College of Art and Design."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, released as a single from "Different Class," became an immense phenomenon in the UK, described as "a madness." Despite not reaching number one on the charts, it achieved iconic status and is now an anthem frequently played in British clubs and bars, where it makes people "go crazy." Jarvis Cocker's performance in its music video was particularly memorable. "Common People was a madness within the United Kingdom."
